    Reference

    Models & ensembles¶

    Architecture factories return ready-to-use reservoir models. headless_esn and linear_esn omit the readout; parallel_esn returns a ParallelESNModel for spatial patching, while coupled_ensemble_esn builds the CoupledEnsembleESNModel wrapper. The other factories return ESNModel instances with a configured readout. KnowledgeModel adapts a physics prior for hybrid_esn.

    models ¶

    Premade ESN Architectures¶

    This module provides pre-configured ESN model architectures that can be used directly or customized for specific tasks.

    FUNCTION DESCRIPTION
    classic_esn

    Traditional ESN with input concatenation.
    ott_esn

    Ott's ESN with state augmentation (squared even units).
    power_augmented

    Power Augmented ESN with state augmentation (exponentiated reservoir states).
    deep_esn

    Deep (hierarchical) ESN — a stack of reservoir layers whose readout sees the concatenation of every layer's state.
    hybrid_esn

    Hybrid physics-prior ESN (Pathak et al. 2018) — a reservoir combined with a knowledge-based expert wired in before the reservoir and before the readout.
    headless_esn

    Reservoir only (no readout) for analysis.
    linear_esn

    Linear reservoir for baseline comparison.
    lsm

    Spiking Liquid State Machine — leaky integrate-and-fire reservoir with a filtered-spike-trace readout (input-driven; not a chaos forecaster).
    parallel_esn

    Parallel local-state reservoir (Pathak et al. 2018) — one shared reservoir advanced batched over overlapping spatial patches, for forecasting large spatiotemporally chaotic systems (PDEs / weather / lattices).
    coupled_ensemble_esn

    Build a resdag.ensemble.CoupledEnsembleESNModel of N coupled ESN sub-models sharing an averaged feedback signal.
    CLASS DESCRIPTION
    KnowledgeModel

    torch.nn.Module adapter wrapping a knowledge-based expert f(u) -> u_next for use inside hybrid_esn.
    ParallelESNModel

    The model class parallel_esn builds — a shared reservoir plus a weight-tied readout with patch windowing / stitching and a spatial- autoregressive resdag.models.ParallelESNModel.forecast.
    Each architecture accepts individual parameters for full customization
    while providing sensible defaults for quick experimentation.

    Examples:

    Quick start with Ott's ESN:

    >>> from resdag.models import ott_esn
>>> model = ott_esn(reservoir_size=500, feedback_size=3, output_size=3)
>>> predictions = model.forecast(warmup_data, horizon=100)

    Classic ESN with custom topology:

    >>> from resdag.models import classic_esn
>>> from resdag.init.topology import get_topology
>>>
>>> model = classic_esn(
...     reservoir_size=500,
...     feedback_size=3,
...     output_size=3,
...     topology=get_topology("watts_strogatz", k=4, p=0.3),
...     spectral_radius=0.95,
... )
    See Also

    resdag.core.ESNModel : Base ESN model class. resdag.layers.ESNLayer : ESN layer used by these models. resdag.training.ESNTrainer : Trainer for fitting readout layers.

    classic_esn ¶

    classic_esn(
    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    output_size: int,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    input_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.9,
    leak_rate: float = 1.0,
    noise: float = 0.0,
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    activation: str = "tanh",
    bias: bool = True,
    trainable: bool = False,
    readout: ReadoutSpec = "ridge",
    readout_alpha: float = 1e-06,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    input_to_readout: bool = True,
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any
) -> ESNModel

    Build a classic Echo State Network (ESN) model.

    By default, this architecture concatenates the input with the reservoir output before passing to the readout layer. Set input_to_readout=False to fit the readout on reservoir states alone.

    Architecture:

    Input -> Reservoir -> Concatenate(Input, Reservoir) -> Readout

    The readout sees both the raw input and the reservoir's nonlinear transformation, which can improve performance on many tasks.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    reservoir_size

    Number of units in the reservoir.

    TYPE: int

    feedback_size

    Number of feedback features (input dimension).

    TYPE: int

    output_size

    Number of output features.

    TYPE: int

    input_size

    Dimension of an optional driving (exogenous) input. When given, the model takes two inputs (feedback, driver) and the driver feeds the reservoir alongside the autoregressive feedback. The driver is kept out of the input concatenation, so the readout in_features is feedback_size + reservoir_size when input_to_readout=True and reservoir_size otherwise. None (default) builds a feedback-only model, unchanged from previous behavior.

    TYPE: int or None DEFAULT: None

    input_initializer

    Initializer for the driving-input weights. Same accepted forms as feedback_initializer. Only used when input_size is given.

    TYPE: InitializerSpec DEFAULT: None

    topology

    Topology for recurrent weights. Accepts:

    • str: Registry name (e.g., "erdos_renyi")
    • tuple: (name, params) like ("watts_strogatz", {"k": 6, "p": 0.1})
    • resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer: Pre-configured object

    TYPE: TopologySpec DEFAULT: None

    spectral_radius

    Desired spectral radius for recurrent weights.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.9

    leak_rate

    Leaky integration rate (1.0 = no leak).

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1.0

    noise

    Standard deviation of additive Gaussian state noise injected into the reservoir after the activation. Active only in training mode (a no-op under torch.nn.Module.eval); 0.0 disables it. Forwarded to resdag.layers.ESNLayer. Must be non-negative.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.0

    feedback_initializer

    Initializer for feedback weights. Accepts:

    • str: Registry name (e.g., "pseudo_diagonal")
    • tuple: (name, params) like ("chebyshev", {"p": 0.5})
    • resdag.init.input_feedback.InputFeedbackInitializer: Pre-configured object

    TYPE: InitializerSpec DEFAULT: None

    activation

    Activation function ("tanh", "relu", "sigmoid", "identity").

    TYPE: str DEFAULT: "tanh"

    bias

    Whether to use bias in the reservoir.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    trainable

    Whether reservoir weights are trainable.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

    readout

    A built-in name ("ridge", "cholesky", "cg", "svd", "pinv", "incremental", "rls", "fista", "lsmr") or a resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer subclass. Additional solver options go in readout_kwargs.

    TYPE: str or type[ReadoutLayer] DEFAULT: "ridge"

    readout_alpha

    Ridge regression regularization for readout.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1e-6

    readout_bias

    Whether to use bias in the readout.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    input_to_readout

    Whether to append the raw feedback input to the reservoir states seen by the readout. Exogenous driving inputs are never appended.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    readout_name

    Name for the readout layer (used in training targets).

    TYPE: str DEFAULT: "output"

    readout_kwargs

    Extra readout options, such as trainable=True, solver, state_noise or gram_dtype. Architecture dimensions are fixed.

    TYPE: dict DEFAULT: None

    **reservoir_kwargs

    Additional keyword arguments passed to resdag.layers.ESNLayer.

    TYPE: Any DEFAULT: {}

    RETURNS DESCRIPTION
    `resdag.core.ESNModel`

    Configured ESN model ready for training and inference.

    Examples:

    Simple usage with defaults:

    >>> from resdag.models import classic_esn
>>> import torch
>>> model = classic_esn(100, 1, 1)

    With custom topology and initializer:

    >>> model = classic_esn(
...     reservoir_size=400,
...     feedback_size=1,
...     output_size=1,
...     topology=("watts_strogatz", {"k": 6, "p": 0.1}),
...     feedback_initializer="pseudo_diagonal",
...     spectral_radius=0.9,
...     leak_rate=0.5,
... )

    Forward pass:

    >>> x = torch.randn(4, 50, 1)  # (batch, time, features)
>>> y = model(x)
    See Also

    resdag.models.ott_esn : OTT ESN variant resdag.models.linear_esn : Linear ESN variant resdag.training.ESNTrainer : Trainer for fitting readouts

    @record_recipe("classic")
def classic_esn(
    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    output_size: int,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    input_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    # Reservoir params
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.9,
    leak_rate: float = 1.0,
    noise: float = 0.0,
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    activation: str = "tanh",
    bias: bool = True,
    trainable: bool = False,
    # Readout params
    readout: ReadoutSpec = "ridge",
    readout_alpha: float = 1e-6,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    input_to_readout: bool = True,
    # Extra reservoir kwargs
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any,
) -> ESNModel:
    """Build a classic Echo State Network (ESN) model.

    By default, this architecture concatenates the input with the reservoir
    output before passing to the readout layer. Set `input_to_readout=False`
    to fit the readout on reservoir states alone.

    Architecture:

    ```text
    Input -> Reservoir -> Concatenate(Input, Reservoir) -> Readout
    ```

    The readout sees both the raw input and the reservoir's nonlinear
    transformation, which can improve performance on many tasks.

    Parameters
    ----------
    reservoir_size : int
        Number of units in the reservoir.
    feedback_size : int
        Number of feedback features (input dimension).
    output_size : int
        Number of output features.
    input_size : int or None, optional
        Dimension of an optional driving (exogenous) input.  When given, the
        model takes two inputs `(feedback, driver)` and the driver feeds the
        reservoir alongside the autoregressive feedback.  The driver is kept out
        of the input concatenation, so the readout `in_features` is
        `feedback_size + reservoir_size` when `input_to_readout=True` and
        `reservoir_size` otherwise. `None` (default) builds a
        feedback-only model, unchanged from previous behavior.
    input_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for the driving-input weights.  Same accepted forms as
        `feedback_initializer`.  Only used when `input_size` is given.
    topology : TopologySpec, optional
        Topology for recurrent weights. Accepts:

        - str: Registry name (e.g., `"erdos_renyi"`)
        - tuple: (name, params) like `("watts_strogatz", {"k": 6, "p": 0.1})`
        - `resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer`: Pre-configured object
    spectral_radius : float, default=0.9
        Desired spectral radius for recurrent weights.
    leak_rate : float, default=1.0
        Leaky integration rate (1.0 = no leak).
    noise : float, default=0.0
        Standard deviation of additive Gaussian state noise injected into the
        reservoir after the activation.  Active only in training mode (a no-op
        under `torch.nn.Module.eval`); `0.0` disables it.  Forwarded to
        `resdag.layers.ESNLayer`.  Must be non-negative.
    feedback_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for feedback weights. Accepts:

        - str: Registry name (e.g., `"pseudo_diagonal"`)
        - tuple: (name, params) like `("chebyshev", {"p": 0.5})`
        - `resdag.init.input_feedback.InputFeedbackInitializer`: Pre-configured object
    activation : str, default="tanh"
        Activation function (`"tanh"`, `"relu"`, `"sigmoid"`, `"identity"`).
    bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to use bias in the reservoir.
    trainable : bool, default=False
        Whether reservoir weights are trainable.
    readout : str or type[ReadoutLayer], default="ridge"
        A built-in name (`"ridge"`, `"cholesky"`, `"cg"`, `"svd"`,
        `"pinv"`, `"incremental"`, `"rls"`, `"fista"`, `"lsmr"`) or a
        `resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer` subclass. Additional
        solver options go in `readout_kwargs`.
    readout_alpha : float, default=1e-6
        Ridge regression regularization for readout.
    readout_bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to use bias in the readout.
    input_to_readout : bool, default=True
        Whether to append the raw feedback input to the reservoir states seen
        by the readout. Exogenous driving inputs are never appended.
    readout_name : str, default="output"
        Name for the readout layer (used in training targets).
    readout_kwargs : dict, optional
        Extra readout options, such as `trainable=True`, `solver`,
        `state_noise` or `gram_dtype`. Architecture dimensions are fixed.
    **reservoir_kwargs : Any
        Additional keyword arguments passed to `resdag.layers.ESNLayer`.

    Returns
    -------
    `resdag.core.ESNModel`
        Configured ESN model ready for training and inference.

    Examples
    --------
    Simple usage with defaults:

    >>> from resdag.models import classic_esn
    >>> import torch
    >>> model = classic_esn(100, 1, 1)

    With custom topology and initializer:

    >>> model = classic_esn(
    ...     reservoir_size=400,
    ...     feedback_size=1,
    ...     output_size=1,
    ...     topology=("watts_strogatz", {"k": 6, "p": 0.1}),
    ...     feedback_initializer="pseudo_diagonal",
    ...     spectral_radius=0.9,
    ...     leak_rate=0.5,
    ... )

    Forward pass:

    >>> x = torch.randn(4, 50, 1)  # (batch, time, features)
    >>> y = model(x)

    See Also
    --------
    `resdag.models.ott_esn` : OTT ESN variant
    `resdag.models.linear_esn` : Linear ESN variant
    `resdag.training.ESNTrainer` : Trainer for fitting readouts
    """
    if type(input_to_readout) is not bool:
        raise TypeError("input_to_readout must be a bool")
    return _esn_builder(
        reservoir_size=reservoir_size,
        feedback_size=feedback_size,
        output_size=output_size,
        augment=None,
        concat_input=input_to_readout,
        input_size=input_size,
        input_initializer=input_initializer,
        topology=topology,
        spectral_radius=spectral_radius,
        leak_rate=leak_rate,
        noise=noise,
        feedback_initializer=feedback_initializer,
        activation=activation,
        bias=bias,
        trainable=trainable,
        readout=readout,
        readout_alpha=readout_alpha,
        readout_bias=readout_bias,
        readout_name=readout_name,
        readout_kwargs=readout_kwargs,
        **reservoir_kwargs,
    )

    coupled_ensemble_esn ¶

    coupled_ensemble_esn(
    n_models: int,
    model_factory: Callable[..., ESNModel] = ott_esn,
    aggregate: str | Module = "mean",
    seed: int | None = None,
    **model_kwargs: Any
) -> CoupledEnsembleESNModel

    Build a coupled ensemble of N independently-initialized ESN models.

    Each sub-model is created by calling model_factory(**model_kwargs) with an independent random reservoir initialization, providing the diversity needed for ensemble averaging to be beneficial.

    During autoregressive forecasting all N sub-models receive the same aggregated output (e.g. the mean across models) as their next feedback input — they are coupled through the shared signal.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    n_models

    Number of sub-models in the ensemble.

    TYPE: int

    model_factory

    Factory that creates one resdag.core.ESNModel. All keyword arguments not consumed by coupled_ensemble_esn itself (i.e. model_kwargs) are forwarded verbatim to every call of this factory. The factory must return a readout-bearing model whose first output dimension equals the feedback input dimension, so the aggregated output can be fed back autoregressively. The readout-bearing premade factories — classic_esn, ott_esn and power_augmented — satisfy this. The headless factories (headless_esn, linear_esn) emit raw reservoir states rather than a feedback-dimensioned output and are rejected by resdag.ensemble.CoupledEnsembleESNModel (see its __init__ for the exact check).

    TYPE: callable DEFAULT: `ott_esn`

    aggregate

    Aggregation strategy applied to the N model outputs at each autoregressive step:

    • "mean" — arithmetic mean.
    • "median" — median.
    • nn.Module — any module accepting a stacked tensor of shape (N, batch, timesteps, features) and returning (batch, timesteps, features). E.g. resdag.ensemble.aggregators.OutliersFilteredMean.

    TYPE: str or Module DEFAULT: `"mean"`

    seed

    Master seed for deterministic sub-model construction. Sub-model i is seeded with seed + i immediately before the factory call. If model_factory itself accepts a seed keyword argument, seed + i is also forwarded as that argument so initialisers that take an explicit seed (e.g. graph topologies) become reproducible.

    CPU, available MPS and initialized/requested CUDA RNG states are restored on exit, even if a factory raises. MPS isolation may materialize its host-side generator, but does not create MPS tensors or streams for a CPU factory. Unavailable accelerators and unused CUDA runtimes are not initialized. Subsequent random draws in a larger pipeline are preserved.

    TYPE: int DEFAULT: None

    **model_kwargs

    All remaining keyword arguments are forwarded verbatim to each model_factory call. This includes architecture parameters such as reservoir_size, feedback_size, output_size, spectral_radius, readout_alpha, readout_name, etc. The exact set of valid keys depends on the chosen model_factory.

    TYPE: Any DEFAULT: {}

    RETURNS DESCRIPTION
    CoupledEnsembleESNModel

    Ensemble ready for training and forecasting.

    Examples:

    Quick start with default Ott's ESN sub-models:

    >>> import resdag as rd
>>>
>>> ensemble = rd.coupled_ensemble_esn(
...     n_models=5,
...     reservoir_size=300,
...     feedback_size=3,
...     output_size=3,
... )
>>> ensemble.fit((warmup,), (train,), {"output": targets})
>>> ensemble.reset_reservoirs()
>>> preds = ensemble.forecast(forecast_warmup, horizon=200)
>>> preds.shape
torch.Size([1, 200, 3])

    Using classic_esn as the base architecture:

    >>> from resdag.models import classic_esn
>>> ensemble = rd.coupled_ensemble_esn(
...     n_models=8,
...     model_factory=classic_esn,
...     reservoir_size=500,
...     feedback_size=3,
...     output_size=3,
...     spectral_radius=0.95,
...     readout_alpha=1e-7,
... )

    Outlier-robust aggregation:

    >>> from resdag.ensemble.aggregators import OutliersFilteredMean
>>> ensemble = rd.coupled_ensemble_esn(
...     n_models=10,
...     reservoir_size=300,
...     feedback_size=3,
...     output_size=3,
...     aggregate=OutliersFilteredMean(method="z_score", threshold=2.0),
... )

    Recovering individual sub-model trajectories for post-hoc analysis:

    >>> ensemble.reset_reservoirs()
>>> preds, individuals = ensemble.forecast(
...     forecast_warmup, horizon=200, return_individuals=True
... )
>>> preds.shape          # averaged forecast
torch.Size([1, 200, 3])
>>> len(individuals)     # one tensor per sub-model
10
>>> individuals[0].shape
torch.Size([1, 200, 3])
    See Also

    CoupledEnsembleESNModel : The ensemble class with full API documentation. resdag.ensemble.aggregators.OutliersFilteredMean : Outlier-robust aggregation layer. resdag.models.ott_esn : Default sub-model factory.

    def coupled_ensemble_esn(
    n_models: int,
    model_factory: Callable[..., ESNModel] = ott_esn,
    aggregate: str | nn.Module = "mean",
    seed: int | None = None,
    **model_kwargs: Any,
) -> CoupledEnsembleESNModel:
    """Build a coupled ensemble of N independently-initialized ESN models.

    Each sub-model is created by calling `model_factory(**model_kwargs)`
    with an independent random reservoir initialization, providing the
    diversity needed for ensemble averaging to be beneficial.

    During autoregressive forecasting all N sub-models receive the **same
    aggregated output** (e.g. the mean across models) as their next feedback
    input — they are coupled through the shared signal.

    Parameters
    ----------
    n_models : int
        Number of sub-models in the ensemble.
    model_factory : callable, default `ott_esn`
        Factory that creates one `resdag.core.ESNModel`.
        All keyword arguments not consumed by `coupled_ensemble_esn` itself
        (i.e. `model_kwargs`) are forwarded verbatim to every call of this
        factory.  The factory must return a **readout-bearing** model whose
        first output dimension equals the feedback input dimension, so the
        aggregated output can be fed back autoregressively.  The readout-bearing
        premade factories — `classic_esn`, `ott_esn` and `power_augmented`
        — satisfy this.  The headless factories (`headless_esn`,
        `linear_esn`) emit raw reservoir states rather than a
        feedback-dimensioned output and are rejected by
        `resdag.ensemble.CoupledEnsembleESNModel` (see its `__init__`
        for the exact check).
    aggregate : str or nn.Module, default `"mean"`
        Aggregation strategy applied to the N model outputs at each
        autoregressive step:

        - `"mean"` — arithmetic mean.
        - `"median"` — median.
        - `nn.Module` — any module accepting a stacked tensor of shape
          `(N, batch, timesteps, features)` and returning
          `(batch, timesteps, features)`.  E.g.
          `resdag.ensemble.aggregators.OutliersFilteredMean`.
    seed : int, optional
        Master seed for deterministic sub-model construction.  Sub-model
        `i` is seeded with `seed + i` immediately before the factory call.
        If `model_factory` itself accepts a `seed` keyword argument,
        `seed + i` is also forwarded as that argument so initialisers that
        take an explicit seed (e.g. graph topologies) become reproducible.

        CPU, available MPS and initialized/requested CUDA RNG states are restored
        on exit, even if a factory raises. MPS isolation may materialize its
        host-side generator, but does not create MPS tensors or streams for a
        CPU factory. Unavailable accelerators and unused CUDA runtimes are not
        initialized. Subsequent random draws in a larger pipeline are preserved.

    **model_kwargs
        All remaining keyword arguments are forwarded verbatim to each
        `model_factory` call.  This includes architecture parameters such as
        `reservoir_size`, `feedback_size`, `output_size`,
        `spectral_radius`, `readout_alpha`, `readout_name`, etc.
        The exact set of valid keys depends on the chosen `model_factory`.

    Returns
    -------
    CoupledEnsembleESNModel
        Ensemble ready for training and forecasting.

    Examples
    --------
    Quick start with default Ott's ESN sub-models:

    >>> import resdag as rd
    >>>
    >>> ensemble = rd.coupled_ensemble_esn(
    ...     n_models=5,
    ...     reservoir_size=300,
    ...     feedback_size=3,
    ...     output_size=3,
    ... )
    >>> ensemble.fit((warmup,), (train,), {"output": targets})
    >>> ensemble.reset_reservoirs()
    >>> preds = ensemble.forecast(forecast_warmup, horizon=200)
    >>> preds.shape
    torch.Size([1, 200, 3])

    Using `classic_esn` as the base architecture:

    >>> from resdag.models import classic_esn
    >>> ensemble = rd.coupled_ensemble_esn(
    ...     n_models=8,
    ...     model_factory=classic_esn,
    ...     reservoir_size=500,
    ...     feedback_size=3,
    ...     output_size=3,
    ...     spectral_radius=0.95,
    ...     readout_alpha=1e-7,
    ... )

    Outlier-robust aggregation:

    >>> from resdag.ensemble.aggregators import OutliersFilteredMean
    >>> ensemble = rd.coupled_ensemble_esn(
    ...     n_models=10,
    ...     reservoir_size=300,
    ...     feedback_size=3,
    ...     output_size=3,
    ...     aggregate=OutliersFilteredMean(method="z_score", threshold=2.0),
    ... )

    Recovering individual sub-model trajectories for post-hoc analysis:

    >>> ensemble.reset_reservoirs()
    >>> preds, individuals = ensemble.forecast(
    ...     forecast_warmup, horizon=200, return_individuals=True
    ... )
    >>> preds.shape          # averaged forecast
    torch.Size([1, 200, 3])
    >>> len(individuals)     # one tensor per sub-model
    10
    >>> individuals[0].shape
    torch.Size([1, 200, 3])

    See Also
    --------
    CoupledEnsembleESNModel : The ensemble class with full API documentation.
    resdag.ensemble.aggregators.OutliersFilteredMean : Outlier-robust aggregation layer.
    resdag.models.ott_esn : Default sub-model factory.
    """
    # Detect whether the factory accepts a ``seed`` kwarg so we can forward
    # the per-model seed to initialisers that take an explicit one (graph
    # topologies, etc.). When it doesn't, the per-model RNG seed below still
    # controls every non-seeded random draw.
    factory_accepts_seed = (
        seed is not None and "seed" in inspect.signature(model_factory).parameters
    )

    models: list[ESNModel] = []
    if seed is None:
        # No seeding requested: nothing touches the global RNG beyond what the
        # factory itself draws, so no save/restore dance is needed.
        for _ in range(n_models):
            models.append(model_factory(**model_kwargs))
        return CoupledEnsembleESNModel(models, aggregator=aggregate)

    # Do not broadcast torch.manual_seed to unused accelerator generators.
    # Seed exactly the same CPU stream as before and isolate active/requested
    # accelerator streams with PyTorch's standard context manager.
    target = torch.device(model_kwargs.get("device") or torch.get_default_device())
    cuda_devices = list(range(torch.cuda.device_count())) if torch.cuda.is_initialized() else []
    if target.type == "cuda" and torch.cuda.is_available():
        index = target.index if target.index is not None else torch.cuda.current_device()
        if index not in cuda_devices:
            cuda_devices.append(index)
    # MPS exposes no reliable initialized-state query: native random operations
    # need not populate Python's generator cache. Fork its available generator
    # using the public API; snapshotting that state is host-side bookkeeping.
    isolate_mps = torch.backends.mps.is_available()
    with ExitStack() as isolation:
        isolation.enter_context(torch.random.fork_rng(devices=cuda_devices))
        if isolate_mps:
            isolation.enter_context(torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[0], device_type="mps"))
        for i in range(n_models):
            sub_seed = seed + i
            torch.default_generator.manual_seed(sub_seed)
            for index in cuda_devices:
                torch.cuda.default_generators[index].manual_seed(sub_seed)
            if isolate_mps:
                torch.mps.manual_seed(sub_seed)
            kwargs = dict(model_kwargs)
            if factory_accepts_seed:
                kwargs.setdefault("seed", sub_seed)
            models.append(model_factory(**kwargs))
    return CoupledEnsembleESNModel(models, aggregator=aggregate)

    deep_esn(
    reservoir_sizes: Sequence[int] | int,
    n_layers: int | None = None,
    feedback_size: int = 1,
    output_size: int = 1,
    *,
    concat_all_states: bool = True,
    interlayer_scaling: float = 0.5,
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.9,
    leak_rate: float | Sequence[float] = 1.0,
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    activation: str = "tanh",
    bias: bool = True,
    trainable: bool = False,
    readout: ReadoutSpec = "ridge",
    readout_alpha: float = 1e-06,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any
) -> ESNModel

    Build a Deep (hierarchical, stacked-reservoir) Echo State Network.

    Stacks N reservoir layers so that layer i's state sequence is the feedback input of layer i + 1. The readout, by default, is fitted on the concatenation of all layers' states — the standard DeepESN readout — so it can exploit the progressively slower, more structured memory timescales the deeper layers develop. Set concat_all_states=False to read out from the last layer alone.

    Architecture (concat_all_states=True):

    Input -> Reservoir_1 -> Reservoir_2 -> ... -> Reservoir_N
             |              |                     |
             +--------------+----- Concatenate ---+---> Readout

    Only the first layer receives the raw feedback; every subsequent layer's feedback dimension is the previous layer's reservoir_size.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    reservoir_sizes

    Per-layer reservoir sizes as a list (one entry per layer), or a single int broadcast to all n_layers layers. When a single int is given, n_layers is required.

    TYPE: sequence of int or int

    n_layers

    Number of stacked layers. Required when reservoir_sizes is a single int; ignored (but must be consistent) when reservoir_sizes is a list.

    TYPE: int or None DEFAULT: None

    feedback_size

    Number of feedback features driving the first layer (the input dimension of the model).

    TYPE: int DEFAULT: 1

    output_size

    Number of output features. For autoregressive forecast, this must equal feedback_size (the first model output is fed back).

    TYPE: int DEFAULT: 1

    concat_all_states

    When True (the standard DeepESN readout) the readout sees the concatenation of every layer's state, so its in_features is sum(reservoir_sizes). When False the readout sees only the last layer's state, so in_features is reservoir_sizes[-1].

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    interlayer_scaling

    Magnitude of the inter-layer coupling weights (layers 2..N). Each deeper layer's feedback is the previous layer's high-dimensional state, so the default uniform(-1, 1) feedback weights would over-saturate the tanh; scaling them down (via a uniform(-interlayer_scaling, interlayer_scaling) initializer) keeps the deeper reservoirs in their useful dynamic range. Applied only when feedback_initializer is left as None; an explicit feedback_initializer is used verbatim on every layer and this knob is ignored. The first layer always uses the raw (unscaled) input path.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.5

    topology

    Topology for the recurrent weights, shared by every layer. Accepts a registry name, a (name, params) tuple, a callable, or a configured resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer.

    TYPE: TopologySpec DEFAULT: None

    spectral_radius

    Target spectral radius for the recurrent weights of every layer.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.9

    leak_rate

    Leaky-integration rate. A scalar is shared by every layer; a list (one entry per layer) sets a per-layer schedule. The DeepESN literature recommends leak rates that decrease with depth — fast dynamics near the input, slow dynamics deep in the stack — e.g. leak_rate=[1.0, 0.7, 0.4] for a 3-layer network.

    TYPE: float or sequence of float DEFAULT: 1.0

    feedback_initializer

    Initializer for the feedback weights, shared by every layer. Same accepted forms as topology.

    TYPE: InitializerSpec DEFAULT: None

    activation

    Activation function for every layer ("tanh", "relu", "sigmoid", "identity").

    TYPE: str DEFAULT: "tanh"

    bias

    Whether every reservoir layer uses a bias term.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    trainable

    Whether the reservoir weights are trainable.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

    readout

    A built-in name ("ridge", "cholesky", "cg", "svd", "pinv", "incremental", "rls", "fista", "lsmr") or a resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer subclass. Additional solver options go in readout_kwargs.

    TYPE: str or type[ReadoutLayer] DEFAULT: "ridge"

    readout_alpha

    Ridge regression regularization for the readout.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1e-6

    readout_bias

    Whether the readout uses a bias term.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    readout_name

    Name for the readout layer (used as the target key in training).

    TYPE: str DEFAULT: "output"

    readout_kwargs

    Extra readout options, such as trainable=True, solver, state_noise or gram_dtype. Architecture dimensions are fixed.

    TYPE: dict DEFAULT: None

    **reservoir_kwargs

    Additional keyword arguments forwarded to every resdag.layers.ESNLayer.

    TYPE: Any DEFAULT: {}

    RETURNS DESCRIPTION
    `resdag.core.ESNModel`

    The assembled deep ESN, ready for training and forecasting.
    RAISES DESCRIPTION
    ValueError

    If the layer stack is empty, a reservoir size is not a positive integer, reservoir_sizes is a scalar without n_layers, the per-layer leak_rate schedule length does not match the number of layers, or output_size is not a positive integer.
    Notes

    The stack is untrained like a standard ESN — depth adds temporal richness without any extra gradient training; only the readout is fitted (by ridge regression). Depth is not a free win over a single wide reservoir: on a short, single-timescale task (e.g. a brief Lorenz-63 window) a single classic_esn of the combined width usually forecasts further, because one large reservoir already spans the needed dynamics. DeepESN pays off on multi-timescale / hierarchical signals — where a decreasing-with-depth leak schedule (see leak_rate below) lets successive layers specialise on progressively slower dynamics (Gallicchio & Micheli 2017; the layer-specific time-scale separation of Frontiers in AI 2024). Reach for it when the signal has structure at several timescales, not as a drop-in replacement for a wide ESN.

    Examples:

    A 3-layer stack of equal width with a decreasing-with-depth leak schedule::

    >>> from resdag.models import deep_esn
>>> model = deep_esn(
...     reservoir_sizes=300,
...     n_layers=3,
...     feedback_size=3,
...     output_size=3,
...     leak_rate=[1.0, 0.6, 0.3],
...     spectral_radius=0.9,
... )

    Explicit per-layer sizes (narrowing with depth), reading out from the last layer only::

    >>> model = deep_esn(
...     reservoir_sizes=[400, 200, 100],
...     feedback_size=3,
...     output_size=3,
...     concat_all_states=False,
... )

    Training and forecasting are identical to any other premade model::

    >>> from resdag.training import ESNTrainer
>>> trainer = ESNTrainer(model)
>>> trainer.fit(
...     warmup_inputs=(warmup,),
...     train_inputs=(train,),
...     targets={"output": target},
... )
>>> predictions = model.forecast(warmup, horizon=500)
    See Also

    classic_esn : Single-reservoir ESN with input concatenation. hybrid_esn : Physics-prior hybrid ESN. resdag.training.ESNTrainer : Trainer for fitting the readout.

    def deep_esn(
    reservoir_sizes: Sequence[int] | int,
    n_layers: int | None = None,
    feedback_size: int = 1,
    output_size: int = 1,
    *,
    concat_all_states: bool = True,
    interlayer_scaling: float = 0.5,
    # Reservoir params
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.9,
    leak_rate: float | Sequence[float] = 1.0,
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    activation: str = "tanh",
    bias: bool = True,
    trainable: bool = False,
    # Readout params
    readout: ReadoutSpec = "ridge",
    readout_alpha: float = 1e-6,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    # Extra reservoir kwargs
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any,
) -> ESNModel:
    """Build a Deep (hierarchical, stacked-reservoir) Echo State Network.

    Stacks `N` reservoir layers so that layer `i`'s state sequence is the
    feedback input of layer `i + 1`.  The readout, by default, is fitted on the
    **concatenation of all layers' states** — the standard DeepESN readout — so
    it can exploit the progressively slower, more structured memory timescales
    the deeper layers develop.  Set `concat_all_states=False` to read out from
    the last layer alone.

    Architecture (`concat_all_states=True`):

    ```text
    Input -> Reservoir_1 -> Reservoir_2 -> ... -> Reservoir_N
                 |              |                     |
                 +--------------+----- Concatenate ---+---> Readout
    ```

    Only the first layer receives the raw feedback; every subsequent layer's
    feedback dimension is the previous layer's `reservoir_size`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    reservoir_sizes : sequence of int or int
        Per-layer reservoir sizes as a list (one entry per layer), or a single
        int broadcast to all `n_layers` layers.  When a single int is given,
        `n_layers` is required.
    n_layers : int or None, optional
        Number of stacked layers.  Required when `reservoir_sizes` is a single
        int; ignored (but must be consistent) when `reservoir_sizes` is a list.
    feedback_size : int, default=1
        Number of feedback features driving the *first* layer (the input
        dimension of the model).
    output_size : int, default=1
        Number of output features.  For autoregressive `forecast`, this
        must equal `feedback_size` (the first model output is fed back).
    concat_all_states : bool, default=True
        When `True` (the standard DeepESN readout) the readout sees the
        concatenation of every layer's state, so its `in_features` is
        `sum(reservoir_sizes)`.  When `False` the readout sees only the last
        layer's state, so `in_features` is `reservoir_sizes[-1]`.
    interlayer_scaling : float, default=0.5
        Magnitude of the inter-layer coupling weights (layers `2..N`).  Each
        deeper layer's feedback is the *previous layer's high-dimensional state*,
        so the default `uniform(-1, 1)` feedback weights would over-saturate the
        `tanh`; scaling them down (via a `uniform(-interlayer_scaling, interlayer_scaling)` initializer) keeps the deeper reservoirs in their
        useful dynamic range.  Applied only when `feedback_initializer` is left
        as `None`; an explicit `feedback_initializer` is used verbatim on
        every layer and this knob is ignored.  The first layer always uses the raw
        (unscaled) input path.
    topology : TopologySpec, optional
        Topology for the recurrent weights, shared by every layer.  Accepts a
        registry name, a `(name, params)` tuple, a callable, or a configured
        `resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer`.
    spectral_radius : float, default=0.9
        Target spectral radius for the recurrent weights of every layer.
    leak_rate : float or sequence of float, default=1.0
        Leaky-integration rate.  A scalar is shared by every layer; a list (one
        entry per layer) sets a per-layer schedule.  The DeepESN literature
        recommends leak rates that **decrease with depth** — fast dynamics near
        the input, slow dynamics deep in the stack — e.g.
        `leak_rate=[1.0, 0.7, 0.4]` for a 3-layer network.
    feedback_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for the feedback weights, shared by every layer.  Same
        accepted forms as `topology`.
    activation : str, default="tanh"
        Activation function for every layer (`"tanh"`, `"relu"`,
        `"sigmoid"`, `"identity"`).
    bias : bool, default=True
        Whether every reservoir layer uses a bias term.
    trainable : bool, default=False
        Whether the reservoir weights are trainable.
    readout : str or type[ReadoutLayer], default="ridge"
        A built-in name (`"ridge"`, `"cholesky"`, `"cg"`, `"svd"`,
        `"pinv"`, `"incremental"`, `"rls"`, `"fista"`, `"lsmr"`) or a
        `resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer` subclass. Additional
        solver options go in `readout_kwargs`.
    readout_alpha : float, default=1e-6
        Ridge regression regularization for the readout.
    readout_bias : bool, default=True
        Whether the readout uses a bias term.
    readout_name : str, default="output"
        Name for the readout layer (used as the target key in training).
    readout_kwargs : dict, optional
        Extra readout options, such as `trainable=True`, `solver`,
        `state_noise` or `gram_dtype`. Architecture dimensions are fixed.
    **reservoir_kwargs : Any
        Additional keyword arguments forwarded to **every**
        `resdag.layers.ESNLayer`.

    Returns
    -------
    `resdag.core.ESNModel`
        The assembled deep ESN, ready for training and forecasting.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the layer stack is empty, a reservoir size is not a positive integer,
        `reservoir_sizes` is a scalar without `n_layers`, the per-layer
        `leak_rate` schedule length does not match the number of layers, or
        `output_size` is not a positive integer.

    Notes
    -----
    The stack is *untrained* like a standard ESN — depth adds temporal richness
    without any extra gradient training; only the readout is fitted (by ridge
    regression).  Depth is not a free win over a single wide reservoir: on a
    short, single-timescale task (e.g. a brief Lorenz-63 window) a single
    `classic_esn` of the combined width usually forecasts *further*, because
    one large reservoir already spans the needed dynamics.  DeepESN pays off on
    **multi-timescale / hierarchical** signals — where a decreasing-with-depth
    leak schedule (see `leak_rate` below) lets successive layers specialise on
    progressively slower dynamics (Gallicchio & Micheli 2017; the layer-specific
    time-scale separation of Frontiers in AI 2024).  Reach for it when the signal
    has structure at several timescales, not as a drop-in replacement for a wide
    ESN.

    Examples
    --------
    A 3-layer stack of equal width with a decreasing-with-depth leak schedule::

    >>> from resdag.models import deep_esn
    >>> model = deep_esn(
    ...     reservoir_sizes=300,
    ...     n_layers=3,
    ...     feedback_size=3,
    ...     output_size=3,
    ...     leak_rate=[1.0, 0.6, 0.3],
    ...     spectral_radius=0.9,
    ... )

    Explicit per-layer sizes (narrowing with depth), reading out from the last
    layer only::

    >>> model = deep_esn(
    ...     reservoir_sizes=[400, 200, 100],
    ...     feedback_size=3,
    ...     output_size=3,
    ...     concat_all_states=False,
    ... )

    Training and forecasting are identical to any other premade model::

    >>> from resdag.training import ESNTrainer
    >>> trainer = ESNTrainer(model)
    >>> trainer.fit(
    ...     warmup_inputs=(warmup,),
    ...     train_inputs=(train,),
    ...     targets={"output": target},
    ... )
    >>> predictions = model.forecast(warmup, horizon=500)

    See Also
    --------
    classic_esn : Single-reservoir ESN with input concatenation.
    hybrid_esn : Physics-prior hybrid ESN.
    resdag.training.ESNTrainer : Trainer for fitting the readout.
    """
    sizes = _resolve_reservoir_sizes(reservoir_sizes, n_layers)
    leak_rates = _broadcast_leak_rates(leak_rate, len(sizes))

    if not isinstance(output_size, int) or output_size <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"deep_esn: output_size must be a positive integer, got {output_size!r}.")

    # Resolve the readout spec up front so an invalid one fails before any
    # partial construction.

    inp = reservoir_input(
        feedback_size, dtype=reservoir_kwargs.get("dtype"), device=reservoir_kwargs.get("device")
    )

    # Build the stack: layer i takes the previous layer's state as its feedback,
    # so its feedback dimension is the previous reservoir_size (feedback_size for
    # the first layer). Collect every layer's state for the concat-all readout.
    layer_states = []
    prev_output = inp
    prev_feedback_size = feedback_size
    for i, (size, layer_leak) in enumerate(zip(sizes, leak_rates)):
        # First layer sees the raw input (user's feedback_initializer); deeper
        # layers see a high-dimensional reservoir state, so scale their coupling
        # down (unless the user pinned an explicit feedback_initializer).
        if i == 0 or feedback_initializer is not None:
            layer_feedback_init = feedback_initializer
        else:
            layer_feedback_init = (
                "uniform",
                {"low": -interlayer_scaling, "high": interlayer_scaling},
            )
        state = ESNLayer(
            reservoir_size=size,
            feedback_size=prev_feedback_size,
            topology=topology,
            spectral_radius=spectral_radius,
            leak_rate=layer_leak,
            feedback_initializer=layer_feedback_init,
            activation=activation,
            bias=bias,
            trainable=trainable,
            **reservoir_kwargs,
        )(prev_output)
        layer_states.append(state)
        prev_output = state
        prev_feedback_size = size

    # Standard DeepESN readout: concatenate every layer's state. When
    # concat_all_states is False, read out from the last layer alone.
    if concat_all_states and len(layer_states) > 1:
        features = Concatenate()(*layer_states)
        readout_in_features = sum(sizes)
    else:
        features = layer_states[-1]
        readout_in_features = sizes[-1]

    readout_layer = _make_readout(
        readout,
        in_features=readout_in_features,
        out_features=output_size,
        bias=readout_bias,
        alpha=readout_alpha,
        name=readout_name,
        readout_kwargs=readout_kwargs,
    ).to(device=reservoir_kwargs.get("device"), dtype=reservoir_kwargs.get("dtype"))(features)

    return ESNModel(inp, readout_layer)

) -> ESNModel

    Build an Edge-of-Stability State Network (ES2N) model.

    ES2N (Ceni & Gallicchio, arXiv:2308.02902) replaces the leaky-ESN state update with a convex combination of a nonlinear ESN branch and a fixed random orthogonal skip:

    \[ x_t = \beta\,\phi(W_r x_{t-1} + \cdots) + (1 - \beta)\,O\,x_{t-1} \]

    Small beta sits the reservoir near the edge of stability (orthogonal, norm-preserving, long memory); beta = 1 recovers a standard ESN. This factory wires the same input-concatenation architecture as resdag.models.classic_esn:

    Input -> ES2N Reservoir -> Concatenate(Input, Reservoir) -> Readout
    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    reservoir_size

    Number of units in the reservoir.

    TYPE: int

    feedback_size

    Number of feedback features (autoregressive input dimension).

    TYPE: int

    output_size

    Number of output features.

    TYPE: int

    beta

    Proximity to the edge of stability in \((0, 1]\). Smaller values weight the orthogonal skip (longer memory); 1.0 recovers a standard non-leaky ESN. For chaotic-system forecasting, smaller beta (e.g. 0.1--0.3) is typically preferred.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.9

    input_size

    Dimension of an optional driving (exogenous) input. When given, the model takes two inputs (feedback, driver); the driver is kept out of the input concatenation. None (default) builds a feedback-only model.

    TYPE: int or None DEFAULT: None

    input_initializer

    Initializer for the driving-input weights. Only used when input_size is given.

    TYPE: InitializerSpec DEFAULT: None

    topology

    Topology for the recurrent weights W_r. Accepts a registry name, a (name, params) tuple, a callable, or a pre-configured resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer.

    TYPE: TopologySpec DEFAULT: None

    spectral_radius

    Target spectral radius for the recurrent weights W_r.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.9

    orthogonal_scaling

    Gain on the orthogonal skip matrix O. 1.0 keeps it exactly norm-preserving (the edge-of-stability regime).

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1.0

    feedback_initializer

    Initializer for the feedback weights.

    TYPE: InitializerSpec DEFAULT: None

    activation

    Activation for the nonlinear branch.

    TYPE: (tanh, relu, sigmoid, identity) DEFAULT: 'tanh'

    bias

    Whether to use a bias in the reservoir.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    trainable

    Whether the reservoir weights are trainable. The orthogonal skip stays frozen regardless.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

    readout

    A built-in name ("ridge", "cholesky", "cg", "svd", "pinv", "incremental", "rls", "fista", "lsmr") or a resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer subclass. Additional solver options go in readout_kwargs.

    TYPE: str or type[ReadoutLayer] DEFAULT: "ridge"

    readout_alpha

    Ridge regularization for the readout.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1e-6

    readout_bias

    Whether to use a bias in the readout.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    readout_name

    Name for the readout layer (used as the target key in training).

    TYPE: str DEFAULT: "output"

    readout_kwargs

    Extra readout options, such as trainable=True, solver, state_noise or gram_dtype. Architecture dimensions are fixed.

    TYPE: dict DEFAULT: None

    **reservoir_kwargs

    Additional keyword arguments forwarded to resdag.layers.reservoirs.es2n.ES2NLayer (e.g. bias_scaling, seed).

    TYPE: Any DEFAULT: {}

    RETURNS DESCRIPTION
    `resdag.core.ESNModel`

    Configured ES2N model ready for training and inference.

    Examples:

    >>> from resdag.models import es2n
>>> model = es2n(reservoir_size=500, feedback_size=3, output_size=3, beta=0.1)

    resdag.models.resesn : Residual ESN (decoupled skip / nonlinear weights). resdag.models.classic_esn : Traditional leaky ESN. resdag.layers.reservoirs.es2n.ES2NLayer : The reservoir layer.

    def es2n(
    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    output_size: int,
    beta: float = 0.9,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    input_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    # Reservoir params
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.9,
    orthogonal_scaling: float = 1.0,
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    activation: str = "tanh",
    bias: bool = True,
    trainable: bool = False,
    # Readout params
    readout: ReadoutSpec = "ridge",
    readout_alpha: float = 1e-6,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    # Extra reservoir kwargs
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any,
) -> ESNModel:
    r"""Build an Edge-of-Stability State Network (ES2N) model.

    ES2N (Ceni & Gallicchio, arXiv:2308.02902) replaces the leaky-ESN state
    update with a convex combination of a nonlinear ESN branch and a fixed
    random *orthogonal* skip:

    $$
    x_t = \beta\,\phi(W_r x_{t-1} + \cdots) + (1 - \beta)\,O\,x_{t-1}
    $$

    Small `beta` sits the reservoir near the edge of stability (orthogonal,
    norm-preserving, long memory); `beta = 1` recovers a standard ESN.  This
    factory wires the same input-concatenation architecture as
    `resdag.models.classic_esn`:

    ```text
    Input -> ES2N Reservoir -> Concatenate(Input, Reservoir) -> Readout
    ```

    Parameters
    ----------
    reservoir_size : int
        Number of units in the reservoir.
    feedback_size : int
        Number of feedback features (autoregressive input dimension).
    output_size : int
        Number of output features.
    beta : float, default=0.9
        Proximity to the edge of stability in $(0, 1]$.  Smaller values
        weight the orthogonal skip (longer memory); `1.0` recovers a standard
        non-leaky ESN.  For chaotic-system forecasting, smaller `beta` (e.g.
        0.1--0.3) is typically preferred.
    input_size : int or None, optional
        Dimension of an optional driving (exogenous) input.  When given, the
        model takes two inputs `(feedback, driver)`; the driver is kept out of
        the input concatenation.  `None` (default) builds a feedback-only
        model.
    input_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for the driving-input weights.  Only used when
        `input_size` is given.
    topology : TopologySpec, optional
        Topology for the recurrent weights `W_r`.  Accepts a registry name, a
        `(name, params)` tuple, a callable, or a pre-configured
        `resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer`.
    spectral_radius : float, default=0.9
        Target spectral radius for the recurrent weights `W_r`.
    orthogonal_scaling : float, default=1.0
        Gain on the orthogonal skip matrix `O`.  `1.0` keeps it exactly
        norm-preserving (the edge-of-stability regime).
    feedback_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for the feedback weights.
    activation : {'tanh', 'relu', 'sigmoid', 'identity'}, default='tanh'
        Activation for the nonlinear branch.
    bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to use a bias in the reservoir.
    trainable : bool, default=False
        Whether the reservoir weights are trainable.  The orthogonal skip stays
        frozen regardless.
    readout : str or type[ReadoutLayer], default="ridge"
        A built-in name (`"ridge"`, `"cholesky"`, `"cg"`, `"svd"`,
        `"pinv"`, `"incremental"`, `"rls"`, `"fista"`, `"lsmr"`) or a
        `resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer` subclass. Additional
        solver options go in `readout_kwargs`.
    readout_alpha : float, default=1e-6
        Ridge regularization for the readout.
    readout_bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to use a bias in the readout.
    readout_name : str, default="output"
        Name for the readout layer (used as the target key in training).
    readout_kwargs : dict, optional
        Extra readout options, such as `trainable=True`, `solver`,
        `state_noise` or `gram_dtype`. Architecture dimensions are fixed.
    **reservoir_kwargs : Any
        Additional keyword arguments forwarded to
        `resdag.layers.reservoirs.es2n.ES2NLayer` (e.g. `bias_scaling`,
        `seed`).

    Returns
    -------
    `resdag.core.ESNModel`
        Configured ES2N model ready for training and inference.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from resdag.models import es2n
    >>> model = es2n(reservoir_size=500, feedback_size=3, output_size=3, beta=0.1)

    See Also
    --------
    resdag.models.resesn : Residual ESN (decoupled skip / nonlinear weights).
    resdag.models.classic_esn : Traditional leaky ESN.
    resdag.layers.reservoirs.es2n.ES2NLayer : The reservoir layer.
    """
    return _esn_builder(
        reservoir_size=reservoir_size,
        feedback_size=feedback_size,
        output_size=output_size,
        augment=None,
        concat_input=True,
        input_size=input_size,
        input_initializer=input_initializer,
        reservoir_cls=ES2NLayer,
        topology=topology,
        spectral_radius=spectral_radius,
        feedback_initializer=feedback_initializer,
        activation=activation,
        bias=bias,
        trainable=trainable,
        readout=readout,
        readout_alpha=readout_alpha,
        readout_bias=readout_bias,
        readout_name=readout_name,
        readout_kwargs=readout_kwargs,
        beta=beta,
        orthogonal_scaling=orthogonal_scaling,
        **reservoir_kwargs,
    )

    eusn(
    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    output_size: int,
    epsilon: float = 0.01,
    gamma: float = 0.01,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    input_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.9,
    substeps: int = 1,
    solver: str = "euler",
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    activation: str = "tanh",
    bias: bool = True,
    trainable: bool = False,
    readout: ReadoutSpec = "ridge",
    readout_alpha: float = 1e-06,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any
) -> ESNModel

    Build an Euler State Network (EuSN) model.

    EuSN (Gallicchio, arXiv:2203.09382) replaces the leaky-ESN state update with one forward-Euler step of an ODE whose recurrent matrix is antisymmetric (norm-preserving) minus a small diffusion term:

    \[ h_t = h_{t-1} + \varepsilon\, \tanh\!\big((W_r - W_r^\top - \gamma I)\, h_{t-1} + \cdots\big). \]

    Small \(\varepsilon\) and \(\gamma\) sit the reservoir near the edge of stability (non-dissipative, long memory). This factory wires the same input-concatenation architecture as resdag.models.classic_esn:

    Input -> EuSN Reservoir -> Concatenate(Input, Reservoir) -> Readout
    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    reservoir_size

    Number of units in the reservoir.

    TYPE: int

    feedback_size

    Number of feedback features (autoregressive input dimension).

    TYPE: int

    output_size

    Number of output features.

    TYPE: int

    epsilon

    Forward-Euler step size \(\varepsilon\). Smaller values sit the reservoir closer to the edge of stability (longer, near-lossless memory).

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.01

    gamma

    Diffusion coefficient \(\gamma \ge 0\) damping the Euler discretization error. 0.0 recovers the undamped antisymmetric flow.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.01

    input_size

    Dimension of an optional driving (exogenous) input. When given, the model takes two inputs (feedback, driver); the driver is kept out of the input concatenation. None (default) builds a feedback-only model.

    TYPE: int or None DEFAULT: None

    input_initializer

    Initializer for the driving-input weights. Only used when input_size is given.

    TYPE: InitializerSpec DEFAULT: None

    topology

    Topology for the recurrent weights W_r (antisymmetrized on the fly by the cell). Accepts a registry name, a (name, params) tuple, a callable, or a pre-configured resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer.

    TYPE: TopologySpec DEFAULT: None

    spectral_radius

    Target rotation rate for W_r (largest imaginary-eigenvalue magnitude of the antisymmetric part).

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.9

    substeps

    Fixed integration sub-steps per interval. 1 is the single forward-Euler step of the paper.

    TYPE: int DEFAULT: 1

    solver

    Integration scheme. 'euler' is the paper's method; 'rk4' and the adaptive 'torchdiffeq' (requires resdag[ode]) integrate the same field more accurately.

    TYPE: (euler, rk4, torchdiffeq) DEFAULT: 'euler'

    feedback_initializer

    Initializer for the feedback weights.

    TYPE: InitializerSpec DEFAULT: None

    activation

    Activation of the vector field (tanh is the EuSN choice).

    TYPE: (tanh, relu, sigmoid, identity) DEFAULT: 'tanh'

    bias

    Whether to use a bias in the reservoir.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    trainable

    Whether the reservoir weights are trainable.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

    readout

    A built-in name ("ridge", "cholesky", "cg", "svd", "pinv", "incremental", "rls", "fista", "lsmr") or a resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer subclass. Additional solver options go in readout_kwargs.

    TYPE: str or type[ReadoutLayer] DEFAULT: "ridge"

    readout_alpha

    Ridge regularization for the readout.

    TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1e-6

    readout_bias

    Whether to use a bias in the readout.

    TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

    readout_name

    Name for the readout layer (used as the target key in training).

    TYPE: str DEFAULT: "output"

    readout_kwargs

    Extra readout options, such as trainable=True, solver, state_noise or gram_dtype. Architecture dimensions are fixed.

    TYPE: dict DEFAULT: None

    **reservoir_kwargs

    Additional keyword arguments forwarded to resdag.layers.reservoirs.eusn.EuSNLayer (e.g. bias_scaling, seed, torchdiffeq_method).

    TYPE: Any DEFAULT: {}

    RETURNS DESCRIPTION
    `resdag.core.ESNModel`

    Configured EuSN model ready for training and inference.

    Examples:

    >>> from resdag.models import eusn
>>> model = eusn(
...     reservoir_size=500, feedback_size=3, output_size=3,
...     epsilon=0.01, gamma=0.01,
... )
    See Also

    resdag.models.es2n : Edge-of-Stability State Network (discrete orthogonal skip). resdag.models.classic_esn : Traditional leaky ESN. resdag.layers.reservoirs.eusn.EuSNLayer : The reservoir layer.

    r"""Build an Euler State Network (EuSN) model.

    EuSN (Gallicchio, arXiv:2203.09382) replaces the leaky-ESN state update with
    one forward-Euler step of an ODE whose recurrent matrix is antisymmetric
    (norm-preserving) minus a small diffusion term:

    $$
    h_t = h_{t-1} + \varepsilon\,
          \tanh\!\big((W_r - W_r^\top - \gamma I)\, h_{t-1} + \cdots\big).
    $$

    Small $\varepsilon$ and $\gamma$ sit the reservoir near the edge
    of stability (non-dissipative, long memory).  This factory wires the same
    input-concatenation architecture as `resdag.models.classic_esn`:

    ```text
    Input -> EuSN Reservoir -> Concatenate(Input, Reservoir) -> Readout
    ```

    Parameters
    ----------

        Number of feedback features (autoregressive input dimension).
    output_size : int
        Number of output features.
    epsilon : float, default=0.01
        Forward-Euler step size $\varepsilon$.  Smaller values sit the
        reservoir closer to the edge of stability (longer, near-lossless
        memory).
    gamma : float, default=0.01
        Diffusion coefficient $\gamma \ge 0$ damping the Euler
        discretization error.  `0.0` recovers the undamped antisymmetric flow.
    input_size : int or None, optional
        Dimension of an optional driving (exogenous) input.  When given, the
        model takes two inputs `(feedback, driver)`; the driver is kept out of
        the input concatenation.  `None` (default) builds a feedback-only
        model.
    input_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for the driving-input weights.  Only used when
        `input_size` is given.
    topology : TopologySpec, optional
        Topology for the recurrent weights `W_r` (antisymmetrized on the fly
        by the cell).  Accepts a registry name, a `(name, params)` tuple, a
        callable, or a pre-configured
        `resdag.init.topology.TopologyInitializer`.
    spectral_radius : float, default=0.9
        Target rotation rate for `W_r` (largest imaginary-eigenvalue magnitude
        of the antisymmetric part).
    substeps : int, default=1
        Fixed integration sub-steps per interval.  `1` is the single
        forward-Euler step of the paper.
    solver : {'euler', 'rk4', 'torchdiffeq'}, default='euler'
        Integration scheme.  `'euler'` is the paper's method; `'rk4'` and
        the adaptive `'torchdiffeq'` (requires `resdag[ode]`) integrate the
        same field more accurately.
    feedback_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for the feedback weights.
    activation : {'tanh', 'relu', 'sigmoid', 'identity'}, default='tanh'
        Activation of the vector field (`tanh` is the EuSN choice).
    bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to use a bias in the reservoir.
    trainable : bool, default=False
        Whether the reservoir weights are trainable.
    readout : str or type[ReadoutLayer], default="ridge"
        A built-in name (`"ridge"`, `"cholesky"`, `"cg"`, `"svd"`,
        `"pinv"`, `"incremental"`, `"rls"`, `"fista"`, `"lsmr"`) or a
        `resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer` subclass. Additional
        solver options go in `readout_kwargs`.
    readout_alpha : float, default=1e-6
        Ridge regularization for the readout.
    readout_bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to use a bias in the readout.
    readout_name : str, default="output"
        Name for the readout layer (used as the target key in training).
    readout_kwargs : dict, optional
        Extra readout options, such as `trainable=True`, `solver`,
        `state_noise` or `gram_dtype`. Architecture dimensions are fixed.
    **reservoir_kwargs : Any
        Additional keyword arguments forwarded to
        `resdag.layers.reservoirs.eusn.EuSNLayer` (e.g. `bias_scaling`,
        `seed`, `torchdiffeq_method`).

    Returns
    -------
    `resdag.core.ESNModel`
        Configured EuSN model ready for training and inference.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from resdag.models import eusn
    >>> model = eusn(
    ...     reservoir_size=500, feedback_size=3, output_size=3,
    ...     epsilon=0.01, gamma=0.01,
    ... )

    See Also
    --------
    resdag.models.es2n : Edge-of-Stability State Network (discrete orthogonal skip).
    resdag.models.classic_esn : Traditional leaky ESN.
    resdag.layers.reservoirs.eusn.EuSNLayer : The reservoir layer.
    """
    return _esn_builder(
        reservoir_size=reservoir_size,
        feedback_size=feedback_size,
        output_size=output_size,
        augment=None,
        concat_input=True,
        input_size=input_size,
        input_initializer=input_initializer,
        reservoir_cls=EuSNLayer,
        topology=topology,
        spectral_radius=spectral_radius,
        feedback_initializer=feedback_initializer,
        activation=activation,
        bias=bias,
        trainable=trainable,
        readout=readout,
        readout_alpha=readout_alpha,
        readout_bias=readout_bias,
        readout_name=readout_name,
        readout_kwargs=readout_kwargs,
        epsilon=epsilon,
        gamma=gamma,
        substeps=substeps,
        solver=solver,
        **reservoir_kwargs,
    )

    def gated_esn(
    reservoir_size: int,
    feedback_size: int,
    output_size: int,
    input_size: int | None = None,
    input_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    # Reservoir params
    topology: TopologySpec | None = None,
    spectral_radius: float = 0.9,
    update_gate_bias: float = 2.0,
    activation: str = "relu",
    gate_activation: str = "sigmoid",
    feedback_initializer: InitializerSpec | None = None,
    bias: bool = True,
    trainable: bool = False,
    concat_input: bool = True,
    # Readout params
    readout: ReadoutSpec = "ridge",
    readout_alpha: float = 1e-6,
    readout_bias: bool = True,
    readout_name: str = "output",
    readout_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    # Extra reservoir kwargs
    **reservoir_kwargs: Any,
) -> ESNModel:
    """Build a gated ("reservoir GRU") ESN model.

    The reservoir is a frozen (or trainable) LiGRU-style gated recurrent cell.
    The raw input is concatenated with the reservoir output before the readout,
    following the classic-ESN wiring:

    ```text
    Input -> GatedReservoirLayer -> Concatenate(Input, Reservoir) -> Readout
    ```

    Parameters
    ----------
    reservoir_size : int
        Number of units in the reservoir.
    feedback_size : int
        Number of feedback features (input dimension).
    output_size : int
        Number of output features.
    input_size : int or None, optional
        Dimension of an optional driving (exogenous) input.  When given, the
        model takes two inputs `(feedback, driver)`; the driver feeds the
        reservoir but is kept out of the input concatenation, so the readout
        `in_features` stays `feedback_size + reservoir_size`.
    input_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for the driving-input weights.  Only used when `input_size`
        is given.
    topology : TopologySpec, optional
        Topology for the recurrent **candidate** weight.  The update-gate
        recurrent weight is always dense-random.
    spectral_radius : float, default=0.9
        Desired spectral radius for the recurrent candidate weight.
    update_gate_bias : float, default=2.0
        Retention bias on the update gate (keeps a frozen gated reservoir from
        washing out its memory).  See
        `resdag.layers.cells.gated_cell.GatedReservoirCell`.
    activation : str, default="relu"
        Candidate nonlinearity (LiGRU default is `"relu"`).
    gate_activation : str, default="sigmoid"
        Update-gate nonlinearity.
    feedback_initializer : InitializerSpec, optional
        Initializer for feedback weights.
    bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to use gate biases in the reservoir.
    trainable : bool, default=False
        Whether reservoir weights are trainable.  A frozen gated reservoir often
        underperforms an ESN; `True` (BPTT through the gates) is frequently the
        more useful setting.  Note the ReLU candidate is unbounded, so a *frozen*
        autoregressive forecast that drifts off the attractor can grow large in
        magnitude (not merely track poorly) — prefer `trainable=True` for
        closed-loop forecasting.
    concat_input : bool, default=True
        Whether to concatenate the raw input with the reservoir output before the
        readout.
    readout : str or type[ReadoutLayer], default="ridge"
        A built-in name (`"ridge"`, `"cholesky"`, `"cg"`, `"svd"`,
        `"pinv"`, `"incremental"`, `"rls"`, `"fista"`, `"lsmr"`) or a
        `resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer` subclass. Additional
        solver options go in `readout_kwargs`.
    readout_alpha : float, default=1e-6
        Ridge regularization for the readout.
    readout_bias : bool, default=True
        Whether to use bias in the readout.
    readout_name : str, default="output"
        Name for the readout layer (used as the target key in training).
    readout_kwargs : dict, optional
        Extra readout options, such as `trainable=True`, `solver`,
        `state_noise` or `gram_dtype`. Architecture dimensions are fixed.
    **reservoir_kwargs : Any
        Additional keyword arguments forwarded to
        `resdag.layers.reservoirs.gated.GatedReservoirLayer`.

    Returns
    -------
    `resdag.core.ESNModel`
        Configured gated ESN model ready for training and inference.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `output_size` is not a positive integer, or `readout` is an
        unknown string key.
    TypeError
        If `readout` is neither a known string key nor a
        `resdag.layers.readouts.ReadoutLayer` subclass.

    Examples
    --------
    Trainable gated ESN on a 3-D signal:

    >>> from resdag.models import gated_esn
    >>> model = gated_esn(200, feedback_size=3, output_size=3, trainable=True)

    See Also
    --------
    resdag.models.classic_esn : The ungated classic ESN with the same wiring.
    resdag.layers.reservoirs.gated.GatedReservoirLayer : The gated reservoir layer.
    """
    if output_size <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"output_size must be a positive integer, got {output_size!r}")

    # Resolve the readout up front so an invalid spec fails before construction.

    inp = reservoir_input(
        feedback_size, dtype=reservoir_kwargs.get("dtype"), device=reservoir_kwargs.get("device")
    )
    driver = (
        reservoir_input(
            input_size, dtype=reservoir_kwargs.get("dtype"), device=reservoir_kwargs.get("device")
        )
        if input_size
        else None
    )

    reservoir = GatedReservoirLayer(
        reservoir_size=reservoir_size,
        feedback_size=feedback_size,
        input_size=input_size,
        topology=topology,
        spectral_radius=spectral_radius,
        update_gate_bias=update_gate_bias,
        activation=activation,
        gate_activation=gate_activation,
        feedback_initializer=feedback_initializer,
        input_initializer=input_initializer,
        bias=bias,
        trainable=trainable,
        **reservoir_kwargs,
    )

    output: SymbolicTensor = reservoir(inp) if driver is None else reservoir(inp, driver)
    model_inputs = inp if driver is None else [inp, driver]

    if concat_input:
        output = Concatenate()(inp, output)
        readout_in_features = feedback_size + reservoir_size
    else:
        readout_in_features = reservoir_size

    readout_layer = _make_readout(
        readout,
        in_features=readout_in_features,
        out_features=output_size,
        bias=readout_bias,
        alpha=readout_alpha,
        name=readout_name,
        readout_kwargs=readout_kwargs,
    ).to(device=reservoir.weight_feedback.device, dtype=reservoir.weight_feedback.dtype)(output)

    return ESNModel(model_inputs, readout_layer)

    KnowledgeModel ¶

    KnowledgeModel(fn: KnowledgeFn | Module, model_out_size: int)

    Bases: Module

    Wrap a knowledge-based expert f(u) -> u_next as a DAG layer.

    Adapts an arbitrary one-step-ahead predictor — a plain callable or another torch.nn.Module (e.g. one Euler/RK step of an approximate ODE) — so it slots into a pytorch_symbolic model and is re-evaluated on the current feedback at every timestep, including the autoregressive forecast loop where the reservoir feeds the model its own previous prediction.

    The wrapped callable is applied directly to the (batch, time, features) (or single-step (batch, 1, features)) tensor and must broadcast over the leading batch/time axes, operating feature-wise on the last dimension — the standard PyTorch idiom. Its output feature dimension, model_out_size, may differ from the input dimension (though it is typically equal, since the expert predicts the next state).

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    fn

    The knowledge model. Called as fn(u) with u of shape (batch, time, features) and must return a tensor of shape (batch, time, model_out_size) — i.e. it may change only the last (feature) dimension. A crude approximate integrator is enough; it does not need to be accurate, only informative.

    TYPE: callable or Module

    model_out_size

    Feature dimension of fn's output. Used by hybrid_esn to size the concatenations and the informed input split; validated at call time.

    TYPE: int

    ATTRIBUTE DESCRIPTION
    fn

    The wrapped knowledge model. Registered as a submodule when it is an torch.nn.Module, so its parameters/buffers move with .to().

    TYPE: callable or Module

    model_out_size

    The declared output feature dimension.

    TYPE: int

    RAISES DESCRIPTION
    ValueError

    At forward time, if fn's output rank does not match its input or its last dimension is not model_out_size.

    Examples:

    A rough Lorenz-63 Euler step used as a physics prior::

    >>> import torch
>>> from resdag.models import KnowledgeModel
>>> def lorenz_euler(u, dt=0.02, sigma=10.0, rho=28.0, beta=8.0 / 3.0):
...     x, y, z = u[..., 0], u[..., 1], u[..., 2]
...     dx = sigma * (y - x)
...     dy = x * (rho - z) - y
...     dz = x * y - beta * z
...     return u + dt * torch.stack([dx, dy, dz], dim=-1)
>>> expert = KnowledgeModel(lorenz_euler, model_out_size=3)
>>> u = torch.randn(4, 50, 3)
>>> expert(u).shape
torch.Size([4, 50, 3])
    See Also

    hybrid_esn : The factory that wires this expert into a hybrid ESN.

    RAISES DESCRIPTION
    TypeError

    If fn is not callable.
    ValueError

    If model_out_size is not a positive integer.

    def __init__(self, fn: KnowledgeFn | nn.Module, model_out_size: int) -> None:
    """Store the callable and its declared output dimension.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If `fn` is not callable.
    ValueError
        If `model_out_size` is not a positive integer.
    """
    super().__init__()
    if not callable(fn):
        raise TypeError(f"KnowledgeModel: fn must be callable, got {type(fn).__name__}.")
    if not isinstance(model_out_size, int) or model_out_size <= 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"KnowledgeModel: model_out_size must be a positive integer, "
            f"got {model_out_size!r}."
        )
    # Registering an nn.Module submodule under ``fn`` means its parameters and
    # buffers are discovered by ``.parameters()`` / moved by ``.to(...)``. A
    # plain callable is stored as a bare attribute (no parameters to track).
    self.fn = fn
    self.model_out_size = model_out_size

    forward ¶

    forward(u: Tensor) -> Tensor

    Apply the knowledge model to the current state u.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION

    Current state of shape (batch, time, features) (or the single-step (batch, 1, features) slice used during autoregressive forecasting).

    The one-step-ahead prediction of shape (batch, time, model_out_size).

    def forward(self, u: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Apply the knowledge model to the current state `u`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    u : torch.Tensor
        Current state of shape `(batch, time, features)` (or the single-step
        `(batch, 1, features)` slice used during autoregressive forecasting).

    Returns
    -------
    torch.Tensor
        The one-step-ahead prediction of shape
        `(batch, time, model_out_size)`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the wrapped model's output rank differs from `u` or its last
        dimension is not `model_out_size`.
    """
    out = self.fn(u)
    if out.shape[:-1] != u.shape[:-1] or out.shape[-1] != self.model_out_size:
        raise ValueError(
            f"KnowledgeModel: fn(u) must return shape "
            f"{(*u.shape[:-1], self.model_out_size)} (same batch/time as the "
            f"input, last dim = model_out_size={self.model_out_size}); got "
            f"{tuple(out.shape)} for input {tuple(u.shape)}."
        )
    return out
